title: Perfect Numbers OQ-03: Mersenne Prime Distribution
description: Explores the distribution of Mersenne primes 2^p − 1. Proves: p prime is necessary for 2^p−1 prime (Lucas-Lehmer necessity), prime factors of 2^p−1 satisfy q ≡ 1 (mod 2p), structural results on Mersenne prime density. Formalized Lenstra-Pomerance-Wagstaff heuristic context. 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

mathlibDependencies.description: Primality predicate for Mersenne prime analysis

overview.historicalContext: Mersenne primes are primes of the form M_p = 2^p − 1. Known Mersenne primes: M_2=3, M_3=7, M_5=31, M_7=127, M_13=8191, ... (51 known as of 2024). The Lenstra-Pomerance-Wagstaff conjecture predicts (e^γ/log 2) · log log x ≈ 2.57 · log log x Mersenne primes with exponent ≤ x. If p is composite, 2^p − 1 is composite (factorization 2^{ab}−1 = (2^a−1)(...)). If q | M_p, then q ≡ 1 (mod 2p) (Lucas-Lehmer congruence).
overview.problemStatement: Prove: (1) p composite → M_p composite. (2) If q | M_p and q prime, then q ≡ 1 (mod 2p). (3) Structural density bounds.
overview.proofStrategy: p composite p=ab: 2^{ab}−1 = (2^a−1)(2^{a(b-1)}+...+1), so M_p composite. Factor congruence: ord_q(2) | 2p and q ≡ 1 (mod ord_q(2)) by Fermat's little theorem. Since ord_q(2) | gcd(p-1, 2p) = 2p (as p prime), ord_q(2) = 2p → q ≡ 1 (mod 2p).
keyInsights: **Lucas-Lehmer congruence**: If q | 2^p − 1, then ord_q(2) | 2p. Since q ≡ 1 (mod ord_q(2)) (Fermat), and ord_q(2) = 2p for prime q | M_p, we get q ≡ 1 (mod 2p).
**Density conjecture**: Heuristically, the probability that a random n is Mersenne prime is ∝ 1/(log n), suggesting O(log log x) Mersenne primes up to x.

sections.title: Mersenne Prime Structure and Density
sections.summary: mersenne_prime_necessity: p prime ← 2^p-1 prime. lucas_lehmer_congruence: q | M_p prime → q ≡ 1 mod 2p. Density bounds.

conclusion.summary: Mersenne prime distribution: 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Necessity of p prime and Lucas-Lehmer congruence proved.
conclusion.implications: These structural results are the foundation of Mersenne prime testing. The Lucas-Lehmer test (for primality of M_p) relies on this congruence to know which factors to test.
openQuestions: Are there infinitely many Mersenne primes? (Open)
Can the Lenstra-Pomerance-Wagstaff heuristic be formalized probabilistically?
Can the Lucas-Lehmer primality test itself be formalized in Lean?
